evidence.quote: No instances of impairment were identified in our May 1, 2025, May 1, 2024, or May 1, 2023 tests.

input.label: SUPPORTED
input.reasoning_summary:
The initial verdict of SUPPORTED remains unchanged. The evidence clearly establishes that Microsoft's net income for fiscal year 2025 was $101,832 million compared to $88,136 million for fiscal year 2024, representing a 16% increase, which exceeds the claimed threshold of 10%.

Challenge H1 (restatements): No evidence was found indicating any restatement or adjustment to the net income figures for fiscal years 2024 or 2025. The retrieved evidence discusses tax positions and audits but does not mention any restatement of reported net income.

Challenge H2 (one-time items inflating FY2025): No evidence was found of extraordinary gains, one-time items, or accounting changes that would have artificially inflated fiscal 2025 net income. The retrieved evidence discusses derivative accounting policies but does not identify any unusual or non-recurring items affecting the net income comparison.

Challenge H3 (non-recurring charges depressing FY2024): This challenge is refuted by E16, which explicitly states "No instances of impairment were identified in our May 1, 2025, May 1, 2024, or May 1, 2023 tests." This confirms there were no goodwill impairment charges in fiscal 2024 that would have artificially depressed that year's net income.

The evidence review confirms that E5, E7, and E8 all ENTAIL the claim with EXACT_MATCH period compatibility and represent HISTORICAL_FACT statements. The computed year-over-year growth of 15.54% is well above the 10% threshold stated in the claim.
